### Contributing guidelines

- [X] I have read [CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md)

### Module(s)

mini.snippets

### Question

I've been using mini.snippets for a while and I love it. The only issue I'm having is with variable transformations.
I've read the docs so I know it's not easy to implement them.
My issue is that whenever I type the "begin" snippet from latex it expands like so
```lua
\begin{env}
    env
\end{env}
```
It's supposed to make a variable transform of the "env" in the middle to "\item" if the word is itemize or enumerate, the problem is it doesn't do anything so I end up with some text that I have to delete before I can write the actual content of the document.
What alternatives or solutions could there be for this? I tried going back to luasnip to test it out but mini.snippets really spoiled me hahah

Edit: I didn't know how to format the latex codeblock!

comment_data.body:
It looks like this comes from [this snippet](https://github.com/rafamadriz/friendly-snippets/blob/572f5660cf05f8cd8834e096d7b4c921ba18e175/snippets/latex/latex-snippets.json#L269-L277). It indeed uses tabstop transformations (which is not even in LSP specification), which are not (hopefully yet) supported in 'mini.snippets'.

So couple of issues to address here:

- It should expand as *literal* `$1:env`, like in the code example. For me it expands initially like this (with all `env` highlighted as current tabstop), which is expected:

    ```lua
    \begin{env}
      env
    \end{env}
    ```

- The best solution here I'd say is to override this snippet with your own. Something like this:
    - Create a file '~/.config/nvim/after/snippets/latex.json'. This file should be recognized if you have [setup from the help file](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/35e1767f4cd7dde51256eabae7349a5283a43cba/doc/mini-snippets.txt#L826-L831) and will be used to override relevant snippets from 'friendly-snippets' (if they have the same `prefix`) because it is part of 'after/snippets' directory (which should be processed last).
    - Populate it with the variant of the snippet that you find best suits the workflow. For example, like this:
    
        ```json
        {
          "\\begin{}…\\end{}": {
            "prefix": "begin",
            "body": [
              "\\\\begin{${1:env}}",
              "\t${2:$1}$0",
              "\\\\end{${1:env}}"
            ],
            "description": "Begin - End"
          }
        }
        ```

        This will expand as before, with all three places showing `env` and synchronized when typing inside `\begin{}`. But the inner one is a separate tabstop that only has `$1` tabstop as default, so when navigating through tabstops you can choose to adjust it or not.

        Instead of `"\t${2:$1}$0"` it can also be `"\t${0:$1}"`. This will stop snippet session after typing inside inner part. This approach might be more suitable if all you want is `\begin{} ... \end{}` followed by typing environment and then considerable amount of typing inside.

Does this answer your question?
